headline: Seven majors above their 200-day line, RSI stretched into greed, and whale coins moving to exchanges anyway
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it's unusually clean today: BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, and BNB are all above their 200-day moving averages, all with MACD above signal. Only DOGE and ADA sit below their 200-day lines, and ADA is the lone asset with MACD below signal too. That's six of seven majors in confirmed uptrends, which is a different market than the mixed, one-foot-in-one-foot-out tape this desk sees more often. BTC itself is up 21.6% on the month, ETH up 33.0%, SOL up 41.5% on the month and 21.9% on the week alone, the clear outperformer of the group.

But trend agreement doesn't mean the move is fresh. RSI-14 on BTC sits at 72.5, ETH at 71.7, and SOL at 76.4: all three deep in overbought territory by the standard reading. That's momentum that has already run hard, not momentum just getting started. Nothing here is diverging yet, price and MACD and RSI are all pointing the same direction, but a trend with RSI in the mid-70s is a trend that has spent most of its fuel getting where it is, worth noting rather than ignoring.

Positioning adds texture. Funding is modest across the board: BTC at 5.4% annualized, ETH at 3.4%, SOL barely paying anything at 1.1%. That's not the crowded, expensive long book you'd expect given how stretched RSI looks. DOGE is the outlier, funding running 10.0% annualized with a long/short ratio of 4.07, the most lopsided book on the sheet, and its liquidations over the last 22 hours were overwhelmingly short-side ($265,727 shorts vs $24,627 longs), meaning shorts have been the ones getting run over. Across every asset on the leverage board, short liquidations dwarf long liquidations by wide margins (BTC: $2.86M shorts vs $14,722 longs; ETH: $1.74M vs $40,929), which tells you this rally has been squeezing skeptics more than it's been fed by fresh leveraged longs piling in.

Now the tension. Whale flows over the last 48 hours show $113.7 million in BTC moving net onto exchanges, and the weekly pattern backs it up: three straight weeks of net onto-exchange flow (week ending Aug 16: $508M onto exchanges, Aug 23: $1,062M onto exchanges, Aug 30: $659M onto exchanges), a reversal from the prior week ending Aug 09 when $67M moved off. Coins moving toward exchanges during a greed-labeled, uptrend-confirmed rally is the kind of thing that deserves a raised eyebrow, since exchange deposits are usually a precondition for selling, not holding. On the ETF side, the picture is split by window: the latest print on 28 Aug showed a BTC outflow of $201.9 million, while the last five sessions net to a $924.5 million inflow, a genuine disagreement between the daily and the five-day view that's worth holding both ends of rather than picking one. ETH ETFs show no such conflict, inflow of $102.1 million on the day and $815.7 million over the last five sessions, with ten straight days in the same direction.

Sentiment reads at 69, Greed, comfortably inside its own 30-day range of 25 to 74 rather than pinned at the top. It agrees with the price action but doesn't add anything price and RSI haven't already said. The more interesting disagreement sits between the ETF story and the whale story: traditional finance's five-day BTC flow is decisively net positive while wallets are shifting coin onto exchanges over the same broad window. What to watch from here: whether the daily BTC ETF print flips back positive and starts confirming the five-day trend, whether the onto-exchange whale flow continues into a fourth straight week, and whether DOGE's 4.07 long/short ratio and 10% funding start drawing in the kind of short liquidations that eventually invite a long squeeze the other way.
